title: What happens when you open a website

scenes.text: What happens when you open a website? It takes four steps. First, you type a web address, like example.com, and press Enter.
Computers find each other by number, not by name. DNS is the internet's phone book. The browser asks DNS to look up example.com. DNS sends back the server's IP address.
Next, the browser sends a request to that IP address. The request hops across the internet to the server. The server sends back the page.
Last, the browser draws the page on your screen. To recap: you type a web address. DNS finds the IP address. The server sends back the page. The browser draws it.
